HONESTY: every quantity is REALIZED or FORECAST. Nothing here is implied volatility.

## Outcome

fvol beats BOTH benchmarks on FIT-era walk-forward MAE in **22 of 24** (asset, segment, target) cells. All 12 SIGMA cells pass — sigma_hat is what the §4(a) bands consume. The two failures are SI's RANGE target at SESSION and NY scope, where raw ATR14 wins narrowly; §3's pre-registered substitution rule is applied there and those levels are built from ATR14.

## Context series (§3) — one named regressor is not owned

| asset | series | coverage | used | corr(log,log) | first date | note | source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SI | GVZ | 1.000 | 1 | 0.451 | 2008-06-03 | used | `artifacts/cache/port/m1/fvol/fvol_context.tsv:5` |
| HG | NONE | 0.000 | 0 | n/a |  | no series | `artifacts/cache/port/m1/fvol/fvol_context.tsv:6` |
| NKD | NIKKEI_VI | 0.598 | 0 | 0.571 | 2023-01-04 | DROPPED: coverage 0.60 < 0.80 | `artifacts/cache/port/m1/fvol/fvol_context.tsv:7` |

**DATA GAP (reported, not worked around):** §3 names the Nikkei VI close as
NKD's context regressor, but the owned history starts 2023-01-04 and covers
only 60% of NKD's sessions. Fitting on the covered slice alone would put the
NKD model's first walk-forward fit in 2024 and throw away three quarters of the
FIT era, so the context column is DROPPED from the NKD model and the gap is
reported here. It is worth closing: on the covered slice the log-log
correlation with the realised session range is 0.57, the strongest of the two
context series (SI's GVZ scores 0.45 with full coverage and IS used).

**DATA DEFECT found in the m0 substrate (affects §3-§6):** one receipt per week
per asset is a Sunday-dated STALE BOOK — thousands of "valid" two-sided seconds
carrying a frozen quote, traded range exactly $0 (231 of 1,417 SI session
receipts, 787 of 4,521 across the three assets). They are not sessions. Left
in, they poison every HAR window that spans them: with a strict full-window
rule the LONDON and TOKYO models had ZERO fittable rows on every asset, and the
benchmarks were silently gated off with them. They are excluded from the vol
history, from the level ledger's prior-session lookups, and from the ledger
build; the m0 censuses already excluded them by other means (SI: 1,174 census
sessions vs 1,417 receipts), so this is a documentation gap in the m0 spec, not
a divergence.

## CC-M1-1(A) expected-move ladder

Built and emitted per (asset, session, segment) in `artifacts/cache/port/m1/fvol/fvol_forecasts.tsv`: calibrated multipliers on sigma_hat for q in {0.10,0.25,0.50,0.75,0.90}, from the trailing-250-session strictly-prior distribution of realised_range/sigma_hat; the regime-scaled twin takes the same quantiles inside the session's vol-regime bucket (terciles of RV_5/RV_66, cut points frozen on the FIT era). Both ladders are registered as SEPARATE level families (`FVOL_LADDER`, `FVOL_LADDER_RS`) so the §6b census decides which earns its place.
